name: Hu & Verdaguer (Living Rev. Rel. 11 (2008) 3, arXiv 0802.0658) Sec. 3.2: for a linear field the noise kernel is free of UV divergences (c-number counterterms cancel in the subtraction (3.12))

source.located: arXiv:0802.0658v1 [gr-qc], 5 Feb 2008, B. L. Hu & E. Verdaguer, 'Stochastic Gravity: Theory and Applications' (2008 update of the 2003 Living Review). Sec. 3.1 p.8 Eq. (3.6); Sec. 3.2 p.10 Eqs. (3.11)-(3.12) and the paragraph after; Sec. 4 p.22 (N_n, H_A,n free of UV divergences as n->4); Sec. 5 p.25; Sec. 5.2.1 p.29-30 Eqs. (5.17)-(5.22).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0802.0658 (page text of pp. 1, 8, 10, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 29, 30, 36)

published_statement: p.10 (after Eq. 3.12): 'The noise kernel is defined in terms of the unrenormalized stress-tensor operator T_ab[g;x) on a given background metric g_ab, thus a regulator is implicitly assumed on the right-hand side of Eq. (3.11). However, for a linear quantum field the above kernel - the expectation function of a bi-tensor - is free of ultraviolet divergences because the regularized T_ab[g;x) differs from the renormalized T^R_ab[g;x) by the identity operator times some tensor counterterms, see Eq. (3.6), so that in the subtraction (3.12) the counterterms cancel. Consequently the ultraviolet behavior of <T_ab(x) T_cd(y)> is the same as that of <T_ab(x)><T_cd(y)>, and T_ab can be replaced by the renormalized operator T^R_ab in Eq. (3.11); an alternative proof of this result is given in Ref. [7, 8]. The noise kernel should be thought of as a distribution function, the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions.'  Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'the noise kernel is finite for y != x ... When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur.'  p.25: Phillips-Hu's expression 'holds for x != y without recourse to renormalization of the Green function, showing that N(x,y) is always finite for x != y (and off the light cone for massless theories).'
published_hypotheses: H-lin: a LINEAR (free) quantum field (p.10 'for a linear quantum field'; the paper's scalar field with coupling xi, Eqs. (3.4)-(3.5)).

H-ct: the regularized and renormalized stress operators differ by a c-number: T^R_ab = T_ab + F^C_ab * I, F^C local functionals of the metric depending on the regulator (Eq. 3.6, p.8) -- true for a linear field, not for interacting fields where composite-operator counterterms are operators.
H-had: physically acceptable (Hadamard) states, for which <psi|T^R_ab|phi> is finite (p.8).

H-sep: the finite statement is for separated points x != y (and off the light cone for massless fields, p.25); at coincidence the kernel has meaning 'only in the sense of distributions' (p.10), and pointwise 'divergences do occur' (p.29).
H-reg: a regulator is implicit (dimensional regularization in Secs. 3-4; point separation in Sec. 5).
H-qf (only for the ALTERNATIVE route of Sec. 5.2.1, not for the Sec. 3.2 argument): free field in a state obeying Wick's theorem (quasi-free), Eqs. (5.20)-(5.21).

rederivation.outcome: ALL 14 CHECKS PASS (exit 0, ~10 s). A (THEOREM, exact sympy, generic 3x3 Hermitian operators and a generic Hermitian state): the covariance <{t_A,t_B}>/2 and the fluctuation operator t_A = A - <A> are invariant under A -> A + L*1 with L symbolic (a regulator-divergent counterterm), while the mean moves by exactly L -- the whole Sec. 3.2 argument, in any state. B (THEOREM, exact sympy Wick with ordered Wightman symbols G(a,b) != G(b,a)): H&V Eq. (5.19) reduces to Eq. (5.21) (all disconnected pairings, including every G(x,x') and G(y,y'), cancel) and at x'=x, y'=y to Eq. (5.22), G = 2(G_xy^2 + G_yx^2) -- H&V's formulas re-derived with no discrepancy. B' (NUMERIC, 2-mode truncated Fock space): Wick's 4-point formula holds in the vacuum to 1.6e-16 and fails in a one-particle state (rel. error 0.82) -- the Sec. 5.2.1 route needs a quasi-free state, the Sec. 3.2 route does not. C (ILLUSTRATION): flat massless G^2 -> infinity as y -> x (pointwise divergence, H&V 5.2.1). D (ILLUSTRATION, flat massless 4D, worldline energy density C = 3/(2 pi^4 (tau - i eps)^8), Ford-Roman Eq. 53): the Lorentzian-smeared variance by mpmath quadrature equals the contour value 3/(2 pi^4 (a+eps)^8) to <1e-8 at eps = 0.3, 0.1, 0.03, is positive, and tends to 3/(2 pi^4 a^8) = 0.0153990 (a = 1), Ford-Roman Eq. 49 -- finite, no renormalisation. D is FLAT: the curved worldline pull-back (Fewster 1208.5399 Sec. 3.3) is NOT run here and stays NAMED.

later_literature.ref: Ford & Roman, 'Minkowski Vacuum Stress Tensor Fluctuations', gr-qc/0506026 (PRD 2005)
later_literature.what: Flat massless 4D: the stress-tensor correlation function diverges as (x-x')^-8 but is a well-defined distribution; non-time-ordered correlators 'have no pole term and are hence finite in dimensional regularization' (Sec. III A) -- agrees with H&V. Worldline (time-only) averaging gives a finite variance, Eq. 49 3/(2 pi^4 a^8); spatial-only averaging DIVERGES, Eq. 50 ~ 1/(pi^{7/2} a b^7) -> the no-new-renormalisation conclusion for a smeared variance needs TIME smearing. They caution (Sec. III C) that setting r = 0 before averaging and the full spacetime limit 'needs to be studied more carefully' -- the gap Fewster's wavefront argument closes.

later_literature.ref: Perez & Sudarsky, 'Renormalization of the Quantum Stress Tensor Fluctuations and the Limits of Semiclassical Gravity', arXiv 2512.17789v2 (Jan 2026)
later_literature.what: For the POINTWISE coincident fluctuation <T_ab(x)T_cd(x)>: 'subtracting a state-independent divergent quantity is no longer sufficient' -- they renormalize the quartic composite by the Hollands-Wald OPE (free scalar, Hadamard states), and argue its ambiguities 'appear not to exceed' those of <T_ab> and 'should cancel' in Delta(T T). In their prescription Minkowski-vacuum pointwise fluctuations are set to zero, whereas the time-smeared vacuum variance (Ford-Roman, check D) is strictly positive: pointwise-renormalized and smeared variances are different objects. Does NOT contradict H&V 3.2 (separated points / distributional) nor the tree's smeared claim; it confirms that 'no NEW renormalisation' is false for the pointwise variance, so the flag must be read as smeared-only.

lacked_data: The result is structural (operator algebra of a linear field plus the form of the renormalization counterterm, Eq. 3.6); it takes no numerical input -- no mass, coupling or measured constant enters the conclusion, so there is no datum that could have moved (data_at_publication is empty, and that emptiness is the finding). What the authors did not have in 2008 is (i) a rigorous worldline pull-back in curved spacetime (Fewster 1208.5399, 2012) and (ii) an OPE renormalization of the pointwise quartic fluctuation (Hollands-Wald OPE 2312.01096 as applied by Perez-Sudarsky 2512.17789, 2025/26). Neither changes the Sec. 3.2 conclusion: (i) extends it to the smeared-on-a-curve case (named, not run here), (ii) concerns the coincident pointwise object that H&V themselves said diverges (p.29). Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: the re-derivation (checks A, B) reproduces H&V's argument and their Eqs. (5.21)-(5.22) exactly, and a 2005 and a 2026 independent paper agree with it on its stated class. Evidence for a limitation: the tree's flag is broader than H&V's class (smeared, integrating the diagonal), and the extra piece is not H&V's.
grade_evidence: The SOURCE stands on its published class: READ at p.10, the argument (c-number counterterm cancels in t = T - <T>) is re-derived as an exact sympy identity valid in any state (checks A1-A3), and the alternative Wick route re-derives Eqs. (5.21)-(5.22) with no discrepancy (B1-B3). No datum enters. What is narrowed is the tree's USE: CURVED_VARIANCE_NEEDS_QUARTIC_RENORMALISATION = False at noise.py:274 and the D22 text at ledger.py:586-588, 1920-1922 are about the worldline-smeared curved variance and carry the status 'H&V 3.2, READ', but H&V 3.2 gives (a) counterterm cancellation and (b) finiteness at x != y / as a distribution on M x M; the absence of a new renormalisation for the TIME-smeared variance on a curve also requires the wavefront pull-back (Fewster 1208.5399 Sec. 3.3), which the tree marks NAMED, NOT RUN and which is not run here either. It is also true only of time-smeared variances: pointwise it is false (H&V p.29; Perez-Sudarsky 2025 OPE), and spatial-only smearing diverges in 4D (Ford-Roman 2005 Eq. 50). Over-representation checked both ways: this is NOT 'WRONG' -- no counterexample to the smeared claim exists, the flat worldline analogue is finite and computed here (check D), and the tree itself states the separated-point limit (noise.py:206-207) and the NAMED finiteness step (noise.py:207-211, 275); the narrowing is of the flag's attribution and qualifier, not a hidden false claim.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS: the flag's comment and D22 text re-attributed as 'H&V 3.2 (READ) + Fewster 1208.5399 Sec. 3.3 (NAMED)' with 'time-smeared, Hadamard state, linear field' as named hypotheses; or Fewster Sec. 3.3 READ and run (e.g. the smeared variance computed on a known curved Hadamard two-point function, Ford-Roman style, with an eps-stability check like check D). -> WRONG (for the flag, not for H&V): a demonstration that the pull-back fails on the curve used (non-timelike/non-smooth worldline, or a non-Hadamard state such as the corridor's, whose two-point function the tree does not have), or reading the flag as the POINTWISE variance (then H&V p.29 and Perez-Sudarsky 2512.17789 make it false). -> OPEN would apply only if H&V p.10 could not be read; it was.
